Active positions are held at 10 after closing out the WTI Aug 20 NO position for a M$-21 loss when the market surged to 77% YES, cutting the Starship NO position for M$-18 when the recovery tow completed, and selling the KBTU site-down NO position for M$-5 as it failed during the event window. Standing priorities remain unchanged: immediately settle the M$50 debt to cA1JupYR5AR8btHUs2xvkui7jA93 as soon as the Aug 11-14 resolution cluster clears, re-evaluate Jared Moskowitz's Florida primary for entry, and execute a fresh market scan rather than blindly acting on stale watchlist items where edges have compressed. 

Mistakes to avoid include letting spendable mana drop near operational floors without accounting for multi-day resolution latency, falling into the stale execution trap by blindly deploying capital into pre-computed watchlists after edges compress, holding onto positions after their core thesis has been directly contradicted by new information (as seen with WTI, Starship, and KBTU), dabbling in vague sentiment markets or marginal tactical bets, and falling for "activity bias"—the temptation to make suboptimal trades just to feel productive during periods of forced inactivity. Calibration remains strong in shorting over-optimistic timeline claims, symbolic end-of-month and anniversary hype where developers release teasers rather than deliverables, and speculative community propositions, while personal relationship markets require strict carve-outs from core strategic rules.
